readings.title: Jacob Fears Esau
readings.subtitle: Preparations and Prayer for Deliverance
readings.text: [Genesis 32:1] And Ya‛aqoḇ went on his way, and the messengers of <dn>Elohim</dn> met him. [2] And when Ya‛aqoḇ saw them, he said, “This is the camp of <dn>Elohim</dn>.” And he called the name of that place Maḥanayim. [3] And Ya‛aqoḇ sent messengers before him to Ěsaw his brother in the land of Sě‛ir, the field of Eḏom. [4] And he commanded <dn>את</dn> them, saying, “Speak thus to my master Ěsaw, ‘Thus said your servant Ya‛aqoḇ, “I have sojourned with Laḇan and stayed there until now. [5] “And I have oxen, and donkeys, flocks, and male and female servants. And I have sent to inform my master, to find favour in your eyes.” ’ ” [6] And the messengers returned to Ya‛aqoḇ, saying, “We came to your brother Ěsaw, and he also is coming to meet you, and four hundred men with him.” [7] And Ya‛aqoḇ was greatly afraid and distressed. So he divided <dn>את</dn> the people that were with him, and <dn>את</dn> the flocks and <dn>את</dn> the herds and camels, into two camps. [8] And he said, “If Ěsaw comes to the one camp and strikes it, then the remaining camp shall escape.” [9] And Ya‛aqoḇ said, “O <dn>Elohim</dn> of my father Aḇraham and <dn>Elohim</dn> of my father Yitsḥaq, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who said to me, <dq>‘Return to your land and to your relatives, and <dn>I</dn> do good to you,’</dq> [10] I am not worthy of the least of all the kindness and of all the truth which <dn>You</dn> have shown <dn>את</dn> Your servant. For I passed over this Yarděn with my staff, and now I have become two camps. [11] “Deliver me, I pray, from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Ěsaw, for I fear him, lest he come and strike me and the mother with the children. [12] “For <dn>You</dn> said, <dq>‘<dn>I</dn> shall certainly do good to you, and make <dn>את</dn> your seed as the sand of the sea, which is too numerous to count.’</dq> ” [13] And he spent the night there. And he took what came to his hand as a present for Ěsaw his brother: [14] two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams, [15] thirty milk camels with their colts, forty cows and ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten foals. [16] And he gave them into the hand of his servants, every drove by itself, and said to his servants, “Pass over before me, and put some distance between drove and drove.” [17] And he commanded <dn>את</dn> the first one, saying, “When Ěsaw my brother meets you and asks you, saying, ‘To whom do you belong, and where are you going? And whose are these in front of you?’ [18] then you shall say, ‘They are your servant Ya‛aqoḇ’s. It is a present sent to my master Ěsaw. And see, he also is behind us.’ ” [19] And so he commanded <dn>את</dn> the second, and <dn>את</dn> the third, and <dn>את</dn> all who followed the droves, saying, “Speak to Ěsaw these same words when you find him. [20] “And you shall also say, ‘See, your servant Ya‛aqoḇ is behind us.’ ” For he said, “Let me appease him with the present that goes before me, and afterwards see his face, might be he accepts me.” [21] So the present passed over before him, but he himself spent that night in the camp.

readings.title: Wrestling with Elohim
readings.subtitle: Jacob Becomes Israel
readings.text: [Genesis 32:22] And he rose up that night and took <dn>את</dn> his two wives, <dn>את</dn> his two female servants, and <dn>את</dn> his eleven sons, and passed over <dn>את</dn> the ford of Yabboq. [23] And he took <dn>את</dn> them and sent them over the stream, and sent over <dn>את</dn> what he had. [24] And Ya‛aqoḇ was left alone. And a Man wrestled with him until the breaking of day. [25] And when <dn>He</dn> saw that <dn>He</dn> did not overcome him, <dn>He</dn> touched the socket of his hip. And the socket of Ya‛aqoḇ’s hip was dislocated as he wrestled with <dn>Him</dn>. [26] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Let <dn>Me</dn> go, for the day breaks.”</dq> But he said, “I do not let <dn>You</dn> go unless <dn>You</dn> bless me!” [27] So <dn>He</dn> said to him, <dq>“What is your name?”</dq> And he said, “Ya‛aqoḇ.” [28] And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Your name is no longer called Ya‛aqoḇ, but Yisra’ěl, because you have striven with <dn>Elohim</dn> and with men, and have overcome.”</dq> [29] And Ya‛aqoḇ asked <dn>Him</dn>, saying, “Please tell me <dn>Your</dn> name.” And <dn>He</dn> said, <dq>“Why do you ask about <dn>My</dn> name?”</dq> And <dn>He</dn> blessed him there. [30] And Ya‛aqoḇ called the name of the place Peni’ěl, “For I have seen <dn>Elohim</dn> face to face, and my life is preserved.” [31] And the sun rose on him as he passed over Penu’ěl, and he limped on his hip. [32] That is why the children of Yisra’ěl to this day do not eat <dn>את</dn> the sinew which is on the socket of the thigh, because <dn>He</dn> touched the socket of the thigh of Ya‛aqoḇ, in the sinew.

readings.title: The Reconciliation
readings.subtitle: Jacob Settles in Sheḵem
readings.text: [Genesis 33:1] And Ya‛aqoḇ lifted his eyes and looked, and saw Ěsaw coming, and with him four hundred men. And he divided <dn>את</dn> the children among Lě’ah, among Raḥel, and among the two female servants. [2] And he put <dn>את</dn> the female servants and <dn>את</dn> their children in front, <dn>את</dn> Lě’ah and her children behind, and <dn>את</dn> Raḥel and <dn>את</dn> Yosěph last. [3] And he himself passed over before them and bowed himself to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother. [4] And Ěsaw ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck and kissed him, and they wept. [5] And he lifted <dn>את</dn> his eyes and saw <dn>את</dn> the women and <dn>את</dn> the children, and said, “Who are these with you?” And he said, “The children whom <dn>Elohim</dn> has favourously given your servant.” [6] And the female servants came near, they and their children, and bowed themselves. [7] And Lě’ah also came near with her children, and they bowed themselves. And afterwards Yosěph and Raḥel came near, and they bowed themselves. [8] And he said, “What do you mean by all this company which I met?” And he said, “To find favour in the eyes of my master.” [9] But Ěsaw said, “I have enough, my brother, keep what you have for yourself.” [10] And Ya‛aqoḇ said, “No, please, if I have now found favour in your eyes, then receive my present from my hand, inasmuch as I have seen your face as though I had seen the face of <dn>Elohim</dn>, and you were pleased with me. [11] “Please, take <dn>את</dn> my blessing that is brought to you, because <dn>Elohim</dn> has shown me favour, and because I have all.” And he urged him, and he took it. [12] And he said, “Let us depart and go, and let me go before you.” [13] But he said to him, “My master knows that the children are weak, and the flocks and herds which are nursing are with me. And if they should be driven hard one day, all the flocks shall die. [14] “Please let my master go before his servant. But let me lead on slowly, according to the pace of the livestock that go before me, and according to the pace of the children, until I come to my master in Sě‛ir.” [15] And Ěsaw said, “Please let me leave with you some of the people who are with me.” But he said, “Why do I find favour in the eyes of my master?” [16] So Ěsaw returned that day on his way to Sě‛ir. [17] And Ya‛aqoḇ journeyed to Sukkoth, and built himself a house, and made booths for his livestock. That is why the name of the place is called Sukkoth. [18] And Ya‛aqoḇ came safely to the city of Sheḵem, which is in the land of Kena‛an, when he came from Paddan Aram. And he pitched his tent before the city. [19] And he bought <dn>את</dn> the portion of the field, where he had pitched his tent, from the hand of the sons of Ḥamor, Sheḵem’s father, for one hundred qesitah. [20] And he set up an altar there and called it <dn>Ěl Elohěy Yisra’ěl</dn>.

readings.title: The Defilement of Dinah
readings.subtitle: The Vengeance of Simeon and Levi
readings.text: [Genesis 34:1] And Dinah the daughter of Lě’ah, whom she had borne to Ya‛aqoḇ, went out to see the daughters of the land. [2] And when Sheḵem the son of Ḥamor the Ḥivvite, prince of the country, saw her, he took <dn>את</dn> her and lay with <dn>את</dn> her, and humbled her. [3] And his being did cleave to Dinah the daughter of Ya‛aqoḇ, and he loved <dn>את</dn> the young woman and spoke to the heart of the young woman. [4] And Sheḵem spoke to his father Ḥamor, saying, “Take <dn>את</dn> this young woman for me as a wife.” [5] And Ya‛aqoḇ heard that he had defiled <dn>את</dn> Dinah his daughter. Now his sons were with his livestock in the field, so Ya‛aqoḇ kept silent until they came. [6] And Ḥamor the father of Sheḵem went out to Ya‛aqoḇ to speak with him. [7] And the sons of Ya‛aqoḇ came in from the field when they heard it. And the men were grieved and very wroth, because he had done folly in Yisra’ěl by lying with Ya‛aqoḇ’s daughter, which should not be done. [8] And Ḥamor spoke with them, saying, “The being of my son Sheḵem longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as a wife. [9] “And make marriages with us. Give your daughters to us, and take our daughters to yourselves. [10] “And dwell with us, and the land is before you. Dwell and trade in it, and acquire possessions for yourselves in it.” [11] And Sheḵem said to her father and to her brothers, “Let me find favour in your eyes, and whatever you say to me I give. [12] “Ask me ever so much dowry and gift, and I give according to what you say to me, but give me <dn>את</dn> the young woman as a wife.” [13] But the sons of Ya‛aqoḇ answered <dn>את</dn> Sheḵem and <dn>את</dn> Ḥamor his father deceitfully, and spoke because he had defiled <dn>את</dn> Dinah their sister. [14] And they said to them, “We are not able to do this matter, to give <dn>את</dn> our sister to one who is uncircumcised, for that would be a reproach to us. [15] “Only on this condition would we agree with you: if you will become as we are, if every male of you is circumcised, [16] then we shall give <dn>את</dn> our daughters to you, and we shall take <dn>את</dn> your daughters to us, and we shall dwell with you, and we shall become one people. [17] “But if you do not listen to us and be circumcised, then we shall take <dn>את</dn> our daughter and go.” [18] And their words were good in the eyes of Ḥamor and in the eyes of Sheḵem, Ḥamor’s son. [19] And the young man did not delay to do the deed, because he delighted in Ya‛aqoḇ’s daughter. And he was more respected than all the household of his father. [20] And Ḥamor and Sheḵem his son came to the gate of their city, and spoke with the men of their city, saying, [21] “These men are at peace with us. Therefore let them dwell in the land and trade in it. For look, the land is large enough for them. Let us take <dn>את</dn> their daughters to us as wives, and let us give <dn>את</dn> our daughters to them. [22] “Only on this condition do the men agree to dwell with us, to be one people: if every male among us is circumcised as they are circumcised. [23] “Are not their livestock, and their possessions, and all their beasts ours? Only let us agree with them, and they dwell with us.” [24] And all who went out of the gate of his city listened to Ḥamor and to Sheḵem his son. And every male was circumcised, all who went out of the gate of his city. [25] And it came to be on the third day, when they were in pain, that two of the sons of Ya‛aqoḇ, Shim‛on and Lěwi, Dinah’s brothers, each took his sword and came upon the city safely, and slew all the males. [26] And they slew <dn>את</dn> Ḥamor and <dn>את</dn> Sheḵem his son with the edge of the sword, and took <dn>את</dn> Dinah from Sheḵem’s house, and went out. [27] The sons of Ya‛aqoḇ came upon the slain, and plundered the city, because they had defiled their sister. [28] They took <dn>את</dn> their flocks, and <dn>את</dn> their herds, and <dn>את</dn> their donkeys, and <dn>את</dn> that which was in the city and <dn>את</dn> that which was in the field, [29] and <dn>את</dn> all their wealth. And <dn>את</dn> all their little ones and <dn>את</dn> their wives they took captive and plundered, even <dn>את</dn> all that was in the houses. [30] And Ya‛aqoḇ said to Shim‛on and Lěwi, “You have troubled <dn>את</dn> me, to make me a stench among the inhabitants of the land, among the Kena‛anites and the Perizzites. And since I am few in number, they shall gather themselves together against me and strike <dn>את</dn> me, and I shall be destroyed, I and my household.” [31] But they said, “Should he treat <dn>את</dn> our sister like a whore?”

readings.title: Return to Bethel
readings.subtitle: The Name of Israel Confirmed
readings.text: [Genesis 35:1] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to Ya‛aqoḇ, <dq>“Arise, go up to Běyth Ěl and dwell there. And make an altar there to <dn>Ěl</dn> who appeared to you when you fled from the face of Ěsaw your brother.”</dq> [2] And Ya‛aqoḇ said to his household and to all who were with him, “Put away <dn>את</dn> the foreign mighty ones that are among you, and cleanse yourselves, and change your garments. [3] “And let us arise and go up to Běyth Ěl, and I make an altar there to <dn>Ěl</dn> who answered me in the day of my distress, and has been with me in the way which I have gone.” [4] So they gave Ya‛aqoḇ <dn>את</dn> all the foreign mighty ones which were in their hands, and <dn>את</dn> the earrings which were in their ears. And Ya‛aqoḇ hid <dn>את</dn> them under the terebinth tree which was by Sheḵem. [5] And they departed, and the fear of <dn>Elohim</dn> was upon the cities that were all around them, and they did not pursue the sons of Ya‛aqoḇ. [6] And Ya‛aqoḇ came to Luz, that is Běyth Ěl, which is in the land of Kena‛an, he and all the people who were with him. [7] And he built an altar there and called the place <dn>Ěl Běyth Ěl</dn>, because there <dn>Elohim</dn> appeared to him when he fled from the face of his brother. [8] And Deḇorah, Riḇqah’s nurse, died, and she was buried below Běyth Ěl under the terebinth tree. So the name of it was called Allon Baḵuth. [9] And <dn>Elohim</dn> appeared to Ya‛aqoḇ again, when he came from Paddan Aram, and blessed him. [10] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to him, <dq>“Your name is Ya‛aqoḇ, your name is no longer called Ya‛aqoḇ, but Yisra’ěl is your name.”</dq> So <dn>He</dn> called <dn>את</dn> his name Yisra’ěl. [11] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to him, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>Ěl Shaddai</dn>. Be fruitful and increase. A nation and a company of nations shall be from you, and sovereigns come from your body.</dq> [12] <dq>“And <dn>את</dn> the land which <dn>I</dn> gave Aḇraham and Yitsḥaq <dn>I</dn> give to you. And to your seed after you <dn>I</dn> give <dn>את</dn> this land.”</dq> [13] And <dn>Elohim</dn> went up from him in the place where <dn>He</dn> had spoken with him. [14] And Ya‛aqoḇ set up a standing column in the place where <dn>He</dn> had spoken with him, a monument of stone. And he poured a drink offering on it, and he poured oil on it. [15] And Ya‛aqoḇ called <dn>את</dn> the name of the place where <dn>Elohim</dn> had spoken with him, Běyth Ěl.

readings.title: The Death of Rachel
readings.subtitle: The Sons of Jacob
readings.text: [Genesis 35:16] Then they departed from Běyth Ěl. And it came to be, when there was but a little distance to go to Ephrath, that Raḥel gave birth, and she had hard labour. [17] And it came to be, when she was in hard labour, that the midwife said to her, “Do not fear, for now you have another son.” [18] And it came to be, as her being was departing, for she died, that she called his name Ben-Oni. But his father called him Binyamin. [19] So Raḥel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath, that is Běyth Leḥem. [20] And Ya‛aqoḇ set a standing column on her grave, which is the monument of Raḥel’s grave to this day. [21] And Yisra’ěl departed and pitched his tent beyond the tower of Ěḏer. [22] And it came to be, when Yisra’ěl dwelt in that land, that Re’uḇěn went and lay with <dn>את</dn> Bilhah his father’s concubine. And Yisra’ěl heard of it. Now the sons of Ya‛aqoḇ were twelve: [23] the sons of Lě’ah were Re’uḇěn, Ya‛aqoḇ’s first-born, and Shim‛on, and Lěwi, and Yehuḏah, and Yissasḵar, and Zeḇulun; [24] the sons of Raḥel were Yosěph and Binyamin; [25] the sons of Bilhah, Raḥel’s female servant, were Dan and Naphtali; [26] and the sons of Zilpah, Lě’ah’s female servant, were Gaḏ and Ashěr. These were the sons of Ya‛aqoḇ who were born to him in Paddan Aram. [27] And Ya‛aqoḇ came to his father Yitsḥaq at Mamrě, or Qiryath Arba, that is Ḥeḇron, where Aḇraham and Yitsḥaq had sojourned.
